question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Din-i Ilahi.
question.text: The Din-i Ilahi was a new syncretic religion promulgated by Akbar, the ruler of this empire. This Muslim empire ruled over most of India under its last major emperor, Aurangzeb.
question.clue: One ruler of this empire created a religion known as Din-e-ilahi.

swap.leadin: This leader was assassinated by Nathuram Godse [God-say] in 1948.
swap.text: Name this central figure of India's independence movement who was given the honorific "Mahatma," or "Great Soul."
swap.clue: With Lord Irwin, this person ended the salt tax in exchange for ending the Salt March.

question.text: Rajendra Chola also defeated this island's kingdom of Anuradhapura. Arab merchants monopolized this island's city of Colombo to trade with its Sinhalese kingdoms.
question.answerHtml: Sri Lanka [or Ceylon; or the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka; or Ilangai Jananayaka Socialisa Kudiarasu; or Sri Lanka Prajatantrika Samajavadi Janarajaya]
question.clue: Failing irrigation tanks triggered the Great Famine in this country's Anuradhapura Kingdom, which fell to Chola invasions.

swap.leadin: In a speech after an attack by Nathuram Godse, this politician declared "friends and comrades, the light has gone out of our lives."
swap.text: Name this politician, who not even a year earlier gave his inaugural address titled "Tryst with Destiny." This politician was the first prime minister of a newly independent India.
swap.clue: In his most important post, he put through the Community Development Program and the 1951 five-year plan, going against the conservative politics of his father, Motilal.

question.text: After Pan Am Flight 73 was hijacked on the ground in this country, Gaddafi paid the American victims $150 million. Another act of terrorism saw this country's PM Benazir Bhutto assassinated in 2007.
question.answerHtml: Pakistan [or Islamic Republic of Pakistan or Jamhuryat Islami Pakistan]
question.clue: This country began enriching uranium in response to a neighboring country's Smiling Buddha test.

swap.leadin: Violent anti-Sikh riots broke out in India in 1984.
swap.text: This operation targeted Sikh secessionists in the Golden Temple. The Indian army has been accused of stealing religious relics during its execution.
swap.clue: Following this action, Operation Woodrose purged members of the Akali Dal who had earlier drafted the Anandpur Resolution.

question.text: This Indian empire, ruled by kings such as Raja Raja and Rajendra, established control over much of maritime Southeast Asia in the early 11th century. It was part of a trio of kingdoms with the Chera and the Pandya.
question.clue: This empire's defeat of the Sailendra dynasty in Palembang was chronicled in inscriptions at the Brihadishvara Temple in this empire's capital of Thanjavur.

swap.text: This country's oldest rock-cut architecture can be found at the Barabar Caves, whose Sudama Cave was dedicated by Ashoka Maurya. This country's largest rock-cut temple, Kailasa, is dedicated to Shiva.
swap.clue: An ambassador to this country erected the Heliodorus pillar.

question.leadin: This leader introduced the second National Policy on Education as part of his policy of improving high-tech industries.
question.text: Name this Indian prime minister who was assassinated in 1991 during a campaign for re-election, several years after angering Tamil rebels by preventing a coup in the Maldives.
question.answerHtml: Rajiv Gandhi [or Rajiv Ratna Gandhi; prompt on Gandhi or R. Gandhi]
question.clue: During his life, he was accused of similar corruption regarding a Swedish arms manufacturer.

swap.leadin: This kingdom's second war with Britain was concluded by the Treaty of Mangalore after the sudden death of Hyder Ali.
swap.text: Identify this kingdom ruled from Seringapatam by Tipu Sultan.
swap.clue: Forces of this kingdom deployed iron-cased rockets with attached blades to great effect at the Battle of Pollilur.

question.text: Gandhi's policy of nonviolent resistance was key to the philosophy of this term coined by Gandhi that translates as "insistence on truth."
question.clue: In 1927, Ambedkar led a protest known by this word in Mahad where his followers drank from a public water tank. This term, translated as "truth force," refers to a form of nonviolent resistance.

swap.leadin: These writings were called "inscriptions of the dharma" by their creator.
swap.text: Name these writings, often inscribed on either pillars or rocks, and whose instances were accompanied by the planting of banyan trees and mango groves.
swap.clue: These documents outline a policy of proselytism towards the neighboring king Antiochus I, though they promote tolerance of all religions.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the Himalayan Kingdoms.
question.text: The Kingdom of Gorkha would be disestablished by Prithvi Narayan Shah in 1768. That ruler would establish this Kingdom in its place, which would last until the 2001 Royal massacre.
question.clue: Chhetris dominated this kingdom's politics, especially after the Kot Massacre reduced its king to a figurehead.

swap.text: The Nizams once paid tribute to this empire that dominated the Deccan Plateau. Founded by Shivaji, it overtook the Mughals as a regional power and fought three wars with the British in the late 1700s.
swap.clue: The position held by the Bhat family in this empire was that of Peshwa, and that held by Shuha and his grandfather was Chhatrapati.

question.leadin: Answer the following about homosexuality in medieval India.
question.text: The Hindu slave Khusrau Khan briefly took this title, succeeding his lover, Qutb-ud-Din. Another holder of this title, Ibrahim Lodi, was defeated at the First Battle of Panipat, and the holders of this title ruled from modern India's capital

swap.leadin: The queen regent Tarabai effectively ruled this empire until her defeat at the Battle of Khed.
swap.text: Name this empire founded by Tarabai's father-in-law, who assumed the title of Chhatrapati ("CHUT-ra-pa-ti"). This empire was served by a line of hereditary prime ministers known as Peshwas, who later assumed de facto control.
swap.clue: A refusal to accept the results of the Battle of Wadagon led to this Hindu empire's first war with the British East India company.

question.leadin: Identify the following about the Pindaris, a group of mounted marauders in India.
question.text: The Pindaris were finally defeated by this first Governor General of India, who was impeached by Pitt the Younger.
question.clue: One of his colleagues Elijah Impey was accused of impropriety by Nuncomar.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about violent events in the lead-up to Indian independence.
swap.text: A spate of politically-motivated assassinations followed after Lord Curzon announced this 1905 territory-changing action, which was more limited in scope than a similar 1947 action accompanying Indian independence.
swap.answerHtml: Partition of Bengal [accept synonyms, accept descriptive equivalents, like the creation of West and East Bengal]

question.leadin: This person's ideas are known today through a series of rock and pillar edicts, perhaps the most iconic of which has a top depicting four lions standing back to back.
question.text: Name the eventually pacifist emperor. He implemented a "conquest by dharma" policy and was the last strong ruler of the Mauryan Empire.
question.clue: Some monuments created by this man were inscribed in Brahmi, others were inscribed in Greek.

swap.leadin: This engagement pitted some turmeric-smeared forces on one side and Najib Khan's excellent defensive formations on the other.
swap.text: Name this 1761 battle in which the light Afghan cavalry led by Ahmad Durrani were finally able to overcome French-trained artillery commanded by Sadashivrao Bhau.
swap.clue: The offensive that led to this battle began when one side crossed the Jumna River and cut off their opponents' supply lines, forcing them to fight or starve.
